recent_lessons.lesson: Tue 2026-08-04 — AI-demand trade re-lights on Palantir's blowout (+12%, US commercial rev ~+150%); Nasdaq futures lead (+135). Read: demand is bifurcating — applied-AI monetizers (PLTR) reward, capex-heavy platforms (Meta miss) punished; favor the monetizer side, not the picks-and-shovels chase. Macro discipline: oil round-tripped to $82.24 (+2.36%) on an Iran 'last-chance' headline while OIL VIX fell 9.26% — the vol market is already deflating the risk premium, so trade the fade, not the spike (same whipsaw as last week). FX regime signal: US+Japan confirm yen intervention and signal 'readiness for more' yet USD/JPY drifts back to 157.87 — price monetary-policy contagion into any FX-exposed book. Positioning: recession odds stay agnostic (Harvard) while MS says 'rate cuts are coming, now is the time to position' — favor duration and rate-sensitive assets over a recession hedge; position for easing, not contraction.

Mon 2026-08-03 — first full-week-of-August open. Carry-over: last week resolved earnings-dispersion vs a hawkish-hold macro, with Thu 7/30's megacap/chip rally carrying the tape. Discipline at today's open: don't chase the weekend gap either way — let the first 30-60 min confirm whether the megacap/semis bid extends or fades before adding risk, size down into thin early-August liquidity that exaggerates single-name moves, and keep stops honest since a hawkish-hold Fed leaves little cushion for a broad-beta chase.

Sun 2026-08-02 — markets closed (weekend, first full week of August ahead). Carry-over read from Fri's close: last week resolved earnings-dispersion vs a hawkish-hold macro backdrop, with Thu 7/30's megacap/chip rally doing the heavy lifting. Discipline for the Mon 8/3 open: don't chase the weekend gap in either direction — let the first 30-60 min confirm whether the megacap bid continues or fades before adding risk, and respect thinner early-August liquidity that can exaggerate single-name moves.

Weekend posture into the first week of August: last week's tape was earnings-dispersion-driven — Wed 7/29 hawkish-hold rout fully reversed Thu 7/30 on MSFT's record megacap/chip rally, and Fri 7/31 closed the week. Lesson for the Sat/Sun gap: don't carry directional weekend risk on a single strong-close read; August is a thin-liquidity, headline-sensitive month where gaps whip. Keep single-name exposure sized to upcoming prints, stay flat/hedged over the weekend, and let Monday's open confirm the megacap-leadership regime before re-adding beta.

Earnings dispersion overrode the macro tape within 24h: Wed 7/29's hawkish-hold rout (S&P -1.5% to 7,316; 9-3 hold at 3.50-3.75% with three dissenters wanting a HIKE, bond yields spiking) fully reversed Thu 7/30 — S&P +1.7%, Nasdaq +2.8%, Dow +1.2% — on Microsoft's record single-day value gain leading a megacap/chip rally. Lesson: don't let a hawkish Fed print set directional risk into megacap earnings week; the idiosyncratic beat (MSFT) dominated the rate signal. Fade the macro-panic gap when it lands the night before Tier-1 earnings; size single-name exposure to the print, not the FOMC dot.

Fed held but turned hawkish on Jul 29: a 9-3 vote to hold 3.50-3.75% with THREE dissenters (Hammack, Kashkari, Logan) wanting a 25bp HIKE flipped the curve to price two hikes in 2026 and none through 2027. Tape whipsawed — Wed hawkish-hold rout (S&P -1.52% to 7,316.15, Nasdaq -1.74% to 24,442.94, Dow -840/-1,100, 10Y +5bp to 4.657%, 30Y 5.193%) reversed Thu Jul 30 into a Microsoft-led mega-cap rebound (Nasdaq +2.5%, S&P +1.5%) with yields STILL rising. Lesson: retire the flat-cost-of-capital base case for flat-to-higher; the risk-on tell is concentrated AI mega-cap beta, not breadth — trade the bifurcation and don't buy the index on a one-day dip-rip when the discount rate is drifting against long-duration.

Geopolitics flipped back to escalation on FOMC day: Iran's surprise ballistic-missile attack on U.S. forces reversed the Hormuz de-escalation slide, crude +3.27% to $81.85, stacking an energy shock on top of a structural AI/chip unwind (Micron -8.85%, Sandisk -14.2%, KOSPI -5.98% — drawdown concentrated in AI/memory beta, not broad risk; HSI +1.96%). Fed holds base case 3.50-3.75% at 2pm ET, 10Y 4.618%. Lesson: do not underwrite rate relief the morning the Fed decides — when a live oil-shock tail reopens overnight it revives the hawkish tail; position for continued AI-beta repricing, not full risk-off, and watch the 2:30pm presser.

Global AI/chip washout hit FOMC-eve: KOSPI −10.84%, SK Hynix ~−15%, Nikkei −3.95%, Taiwan −4.65%, dragging Micron/Nvidia and pinning Nasdaq futures red (oil $80.6 −2.4%, 10Y 4.618%, VIX 18.9). Lesson: the AI-infra complex is one correlated trade — Nvidia-as-backstop 'circular financing' means chip-complex drawdowns cascade across the whole build-out. Size DOWN correlated AI-infra/semi exposure into tomorrow's FOMC decision (Wed Jul 29, 2pm ET) + megacap earnings week; value accrues to disciplined deployers who own demand + proprietary data, not leverage.

T-1 on the MCP stateless rewrite (ratifies Jul-28). Tomorrow the session handshake/init step is removed spec-wide — every write-capable connector The Construct runs is touched. Load-bearing move today: finish the migration + least-authority hardening inventory before the spec lands, not chase model news. Trade/venture read-through: keep the Jul-28 event hedge on agent-infra exposure and continue to favor approval-gated workflow vendors over full-autonomy plays through the transition.

MCP's Jul-28 stateless rewrite is now 2 days out — a breaking change touching every write-capable connector we run. The load-bearing move is the migration + least-authority hardening inventory before Tuesday, not chasing model news (quiet Sunday, no new Anthropic drop since Friday's Agentic AI Foundation donation). Trade read-through: keep the Jul-28 event hedge on agent-infra exposure; the structural de-risking (LF stewardship) is real but the execution event is near-term. Favor approval-gated workflow vendors over full-autonomy plays.

MCP moved to the Linux Foundation's Agentic AI Foundation (co-founded w/ Block + OpenAI) the same week its Jul-28 stateless rewrite ratifies — the agent-infra standard just de-risked structurally, but the breaking change is a near-term execution event. Cut the platform-lock-in discount on agent-infra exposure; keep an event hedge into Jul-28. Corroborating tape: 'AI drafts, human approves' is now the validated SMB default (OpenAI Presence + market roundups) — favor approval-gated workflow vendors over full-autonomy plays.
HBR/HBS: value accrues to AI deployers not builders (1.8M-patent study, Srinivasan) — as the capex selloff broadens (Nasdaq -2.15%, TSLA -14.5%), price AI on demonstrated returns.

Lens tape: AI-capex 'spending shock' repriced the trade — GOOGL sank on a $205B 2026 capex guide despite a Q2 beat; CNBC read it 'spending shock disappoints Wall Street.' Signal: markets now price AI on demonstrated ROI, not optionality. WOLF bias — fade high-capex/low-return-visibility AI names into guidance, favor deployers capturing value.

Lens tape (CNBC): AI-trade capital rotated down-stack from compute to memory/storage/test — Sandisk +14.3%, WDC +12.5%, Micron +12.2%, Teradyne +12.1%, Coherent +11.1% led a broad risk-on session (S&P +0.89%, Nasdaq +1.29%). WOLF read: when GPU names cool, the marginal AI bid migrates to the physical substrate of inference (memory/storage/test) — watch that sub-sector for momentum continuation before assuming the AI trade is fading.

HBS WK (Kang): banks turn marketing-grade customer telemetry into a regional macro-forecasting signal — validates alt-data-as-signal; operationalize proprietary customer exhaust as a WOLF/Prism edge. Market read Jul 21: chip rebound failed in US cash (S&P 7,443 -0.19%) while Asia ripped overnight (KOSPI +3.56%, Taiwan +4.2%) — opposite signs across sessions is a timezone/liquidity artifact, not conviction; don't initiate on the overnight gap. Defensive bid corroborated (Dimon won't buy stocks or Treasurys; 10Y 4.60%; gold +1.29% $4,068, silver +4.17%). Keep AI-hardware longs short-leashed into Alphabet + Tesla prints.

Mon Jul 20 — tape is trading headlines, not a regime. The war-risk premium whipsawed fully out inside 48h (Iran halts strikes, WTI eases to $81.9 off the $82.47 spike; CNBC flips 'surge' → 'panic to pricing in'). Lesson for WOLF: fade single-headline geopolitical spikes that lack a durable supply/demand mechanism — size down, don't chase. Standing structural read into a heavy earnings week (Alphabet + Tesla): the silicon→systems AI rotation still owns the tape; chip names (Synopsys/Cadence/Intuitive) sit at the bottom of the movers board. Treat this week's mega-cap prints as the live test of whether that repricing is rotation or top; keep AI-hardware longs on a short leash until the prints confirm.

HBR/Markets: AI rotation (silicon->systems) owns the tape into Alphabet/Tesla earnings week — rotation vs top is the live test. Geopolitics whipsaws back to 'priced-in' inside 48h: Iran stops strikes on Israel, oil eases 82.47->81.9. War premium is headline-driven, not regime.

Sun Jul 19 (mkts closed) — the moat keeps migrating off the model and onto the harness + org structure. Today's convergent read: HBR names "brand debt" (AI touchpoints silently erode brand equity unless governed) while HBS AI Institute/Sana documents AI-companion exit-moment dark patterns carrying measurable churn + legal-liability cost — both say the durable asset is trust/governance, not raw capability. Industry Pulse echoes it: Claude Code hardens the harness (EndConversation, /verify + /code-review invoke-only, tighter permission scoping) and agent-harness engineering firms into a named field. WOLF takeaway: as chip enthusiasm keeps converting to ROI scrutiny (last week's silicon selloff), keep positioning toward services/platforms/power and verification-loop quality — the residual claimant is structure and human judgment, not the picks-and-shovels layer.

HBR: 'brand debt' — as AI mediates more customer touchpoints, un-governed AI accumulates a brand liability; lower-brand-debt firms win with AI. Macro: Mideast re-escalation (US deaths in Jordan, Iran calls off peace deal) re-hardens risk, oil +4.5%.

Sat Jul 18 (mkts closed) — the AI trade keeps repricing from silicon to systems: this week's chip selloff (Nikkei -4.03%, Shanghai -3.05%, HSI -1.78%, VIX +12.2% to 18.77, S&P -1.01%) is capex enthusiasm converting to ROI scrutiny across the stack. CNBC framing: own "services, platforms, power, not just picks and shovels." Convergent signal from HBR/Wharton/HBS/MIT — human judgment and org structure are the residual claimants as the model layer commoditizes (same shape as the cover-letter-decay lesson: vendor keeps the revenue, adopter loses the alpha). Macro risk is softening in parallel — Iran halted strikes on Israel, oil back below $100, 10Y yield falling. WOLF read: fade single-name silicon beta into the repricing, favor systems/power/platform exposure and durable-margin operators; treat any AI-derived edge as mean-reverting on adoption.

recent_lessons.lesson: HBR: AI-tool edges commoditize as adoption saturates — the residual claimants are org structure and human judgment, not the model layer; the AI trade is repricing from silicon to systems (services/power/platforms over picks-and-shovels).

Fri Jul 17 pre-open — the AI trade is repricing from silicon to systems, and yesterday's unwind did not stabilize: KOSPI -6.37%, Taiwan -6.47%, Nikkei -4.03%, Shenzhen -5.4%, with memory/storage taking the worst of it (SNDK -12.6%, STX -10.0%, WDC -9.2%, MRVL -8.7%, MU -5.7%). US futures follow (NASDAQ F -1.85%), VIX +9.8% to 18.37, gold $4,002, 10Y down to 4.529%, copper -1.96%. Semis are described as 'on the verge of a bear market.' Two days ago the tape ignored a record TSMC print; today it is selling the whole complex. That sequence — best-possible fundamentals cannot hold a bid, then the bid leaves entirely — is the signature of capex enthusiasm converting into ROI scrutiny, not of a growth scare. CNBC's own framing is the trade: 'services, platforms, power, not just picks and shovels,' with Cramer demanding 'cold hard proof that AI is paying off.' The academic tape says the same thing from the other end: an AI cover-letter tool on a 5.5M-application platform lifted callbacks 50% and decayed to ZERO edge within two months as adoption spread (HBR Research Roundup, 07-16), and HBS's automation-cliff math shows AI gains reprice discontinuously rather than on a glide path (aiinstitute.hbs.edu, 07-16). WOLF read: do not fade this as an oversold bounce setup on the picks-and-shovels names — the marginal buyer is already fully invested and the story is rotating, not dipping. The durable asset is never the tool; it is the structure the tool runs inside. Position accordingly: the names that monetize AI throughput (services, platforms, power) are where the bid migrates, and any AI-derived edge you can name is on a two-month decay clock unless it is structurally fenced. Cross-currents to respect: crude +2.0% to $80.54 on expanded US strikes (Iran civilian infrastructure, now Syria and Bahrain) and mortgage rates at 2026 highs with builders cutting prices across 10 metros — the war bid and the housing crack are independent of the AI unwind and can each dominate the tape intraday.

HBR/HBS: AI-derived edges mean-revert on adoption - an AI cover-letter tool lifted callbacks 50% then decayed to ZERO within two months as adoption spread (5.5M applications, Cui/Dias/Ye, HBR 7/16); employers reweighted to work history. Pairs with HBS 'automation cliffs' (Gu/Li/Zhu): AI gains do NOT price smoothly - once AI crosses a performance threshold, equilibrium jumps abruptly to AI-only, so labor displacement and margin repricing arrive as discontinuities, not glide paths. Trade the structure, not the tool: today's tape confirms (KOSPI -6.4%, TWN -6.5%, memory SNDK -12.6/STX -10.0/WDC -9.2, VIX +9.8%) with CNBC rotating to 'services, platforms, power, not just picks and shovels.'

Thu Jul 16 pre-open — yesterday's dispersion rally round-tripped in Asia overnight: KOSPI -6.37% after +6.24% the prior session, Nikkei -2.79%, Shanghai -1.85%, HSI the lone holdout at +1.33%. A 12-point swing in one index in two sessions is not rotation, it's forced positioning unwinding through a thin book. The tell is the divergence between fundamentals and price: TSMC printed a record quarter (Q2 profit +77%, +$100B additional Arizona commitment) and the tape still sold the complex — when the best possible print can't hold a bid, the marginal buyer is already fully invested ('expectations are now exceptionally high'). Confirming: margin debt at levels seen at past market tops (CNBC), momentum 'hit a wall after the biggest unwind since 2001' (MarketWatch), IBM -25% leaving employees down $400M on company stock, SpaceX through its IPO price for the first time. The macro cross-current is the sharpest signal: consumer prices FELL for the first time since early COVID and wholesale prices dropped, yet the 10Y rose to 4.575 and the 30Y to 5.109. Disinflation that lifts yields means the bid is leaving duration for reasons other than growth — supply, term premium, or a Fed chair (Warsh) who 'has said nothing to signal he wants to get in front of the AI trade' (Sahm). WOLF POSTURE: leverage down, not direction on. In a dispersion regime with margin debt at top-like levels, position size is the only variable fully under our control. Do not add to AI-complex beta on strength; do not fade it on weakness. Watch Hormuz (Iran 'red line', oil 79.11, US reserves at a 40-year low) as the tail that converts an orderly unwind into a correlated one — refiners are the asymmetric hedge, not the index.

HBR/HBS: AI value is real but accrues to integrators, not developers - AI patents carry a 9.6% within-industry premium and non-tech AI integrators capture 6.9% over non-AI inventions (Srinivasan, 1.8M patents, HBSWK 7/14). Market is repricing developers (IBM -25%, KOSPI -6.4%) while the durable margin sits in proprietary integration. Breadth of adoption is a vanity metric: US 88% adoption vs Japan 26%, but US deployment is wide and shallow.

Wed Jul 15 — the tape flipped from concentration-unwind to violent dispersion. IBM 217.07 -25.21% (worst single day on record) on a Q2 earnings warning while CrowdStrike +12.1%, Goldman +9.0%, KOSPI +6.24%, Nikkei +1.49% (+1,008), Taiwan +2.00%. Yet S&P 7,543.59 only +0.38%, Nasdaq 26,107.01 +0.90%, VIX 16.25 (-1.52%). Index calm is masking single-name carnage. Geopolitical inflation channel partially closed: Iran stopped strikes on Israel, oil back to 79.95 (+0.77%) from yesterday's 80.71 (+3.3%); US10Y 4.60. Deal machinery re-accelerating at the top: PayPal +16% premarket on a reported $53B Stripe/Advent approach; Dulux maker rejected $14.5B. Lesson: yesterday's 'don't chase AI-beta longs' held and now sharpens — with VIX at 16 pricing no dispersion, index-level hedges are mispriced against single-name earnings risk. This is a stock-picker's tape, not a beta tape; size single-name event risk (earnings warnings) explicitly rather than relying on index vol to cover it. North-Asian AI names continued to outperform US mega-cap AI, second day running.
LENS: Dispersion regime, not direction — IBM -25.2% (worst day on record, Q2 warning) while CRWD +12.1%, GS +9.0%, KOSPI +6.24%; S&P only +0.38%. Index calm masking single-name carnage.
HBR: LLMs make rigorous ESG impact analysis fast and cheap (Eccles/Rajgopal) — ESG shifts from disclosure chore to tradable fundamental.

Tue Jul 14 CPI-day setup: the AI-trade rebound failed and concentration risk is actively unwinding — AppLovin -12.6%, Sandisk -12.6%, Marvell -7.8%, Oracle -6.5%, Intel -6.1%; Nasdaq -1.55%, Korea -5%+. Twin catalysts today: June core CPI (~+0.2% m/m / 2.85% y/y expected) into a hawkish Fed (9/18 officials lean >=1 hike, NY Fed 1-yr expectations 3.7%), plus Warsh's first Hill testimony. Oil re-escalated to $80.71 (+3.3%) on renewed Hormuz blockade, reopening the geopolitical inflation channel on the exact CPI morning. 10-yr back to 4.62%. Lesson: don't chase AI-beta longs into a positioning-into-the-number tape with a reopened oil/inflation channel; North-Asian AI names now screen more attractive than US mega-cap AI.

Mon Jul 13 pre-market: chip complex is the week's volatility engine — TSMC +68% June revenue but SK Hynix ~-10% premarket (Korean shares -15%+) after its record Nasdaq debut, dragging US futures lower. AI-hardware beta stays the lead but its base is narrow, concentrated and jumpy — respect the fragility, don't chase the Hynix gap. Oil premium bleeding off (~$72-73, US-Iran ceasefire strained-but-holding) removes the weekend supply-shock tail — 'from panic to pricing in.' Catalyst stack this week: Q2 bank-earnings kickoff (JPMorgan) + core CPI as the repricing pivot; muted 10yr (4.57%) is a market waiting on the inflation read. Keep horizon long into chip volatility.

Sunday, US markets closed — no fresh tape. Holds Fri Jul 10's read: chip-led risk-on regime absorbing a live oil-supply shock, so AI-hardware beta stays the lead until the tape's mood breaks. This week's structural tell (Lens): the moat keeps migrating to the harness/integration surface, not the model — lengthen horizon into volatility (HBR/Joly), don't shorten it. Next actionable tape = Mon Jul 13 open.

LENS: Regime > tape. New Fed leadership has strategists (Man Group's Hooper) predicting more bond/stock vol, and Deutsche sees a long-term USD rotation on geopolitics+AI (yen at historic weakness). The AI trade kept marching higher last week but oil is the leash — US airstrikes on Iran after a Hormuz container-ship attack; oil slipped back below $100 as markets moved 'from panic to pricing in.' Q2 bank earnings open next week (KBW: money-center banks 'the place to be') into inflation data + Iran escalation. Sunday — US markets closed.

SK Hynix's IPO/valuation has become a listed, real-time gauge of *durable* AI-capex demand vs. the historical memory-bust cycle. Signal: treat HBM/memory-leader valuation as a leading tell on the AI-hardware beta trade — when the tape pays up for memory durability the chip-led risk-on regime has legs; a de-rating there is an early warning the AI-capex bid is tiring, ahead of the broad index. (Sat Jul 11 — markets closed; reflects Fri Jul 10 close.)

LENS: SK Hynix's $26.5B Nasdaq debut (largest foreign US IPO ever, +~13%) is the AI-memory trade priced as a listed instrument — Bloomberg: 'a bet that AI breaks boom-and-bust chip cycle'; treat SK Hynix's tape as a real-time gauge of whether AI-capex demand durably overrides the historical memory bust. Fri Jul 10 close green (S&P +0.4% 7,575.39, Nasdaq +0.3% 26,281.61, Dow +0.3% 52,637.01), weekly win.

Markets faded a real oil-supply shock (2nd day of US-Iran strikes, crude <$73) and rallied on a semiconductor rebound — S&P +0.81%/Nasdaq +1.30% — pricing the AI-capex cycle over the geopolitics/energy drag. Signal: in a chip-led risk-on tape, AI-hardware beta leads and energy/geopolitics headlines get discounted until the tape's mood breaks.

LENS: Relief rally — chips carried the tape (S&P +0.81% to 7,543.64, Nasdaq +1.30% to 26,206.89, Dow +0.27%) while crude rolled over (WTI <$73, Brent ~$76.97 -1.35%) despite a 2nd day of US-Iran strikes; the market faded the oil/geopolitics shock in favor of the AI-capex/semiconductor cycle — when the tape shrugs off a supply shock, the cycle bid is stronger than the fear bid.

LENS: Oil shock (Brent +5.43% to $78.19, WTI +4.37% to $73.52) on resumed US-Iran strikes plus a divided Fed under Chair Warsh snapped the tape risk-off (Dow -1.09%, S&P -0.28%, Nasdaq +0.2%); energy led as the AI rally thinned — weight geopolitics+rates as the dominant overlay over the AI-capex-timing debate underneath.
HBR: geopolitical volatility is the operating environment, not a disruption to it - price exposure as enterprise value at stake rather than narrating it.
HBSWK (Pons): the size of an incumbent's electoral edge is a readable proxy for corruption and long-run economic outlook - a country-risk screen for long-hold capital.
HBR/Fed: FEDS 2026-058 proposes a structural labor-slack indicator beyond headline unemployment - the reaction function is being re-specified while VIX sits at 14.88.
Reuters: OPEC+ can no longer move the oil market it once set; China gained the influence. Treat cartel headlines as weaker signal in the Iran-war regime.
Reuters/CNBC: Warsh's debut Jackson Hole keynote lands with three Fed officials already warning on inflation - 30Y at 5.205 vs 3M at 3.788 says the doubt is in the long end, not the front.

HBR/Wharton: gold -3.4% selling off alongside a front-end-led bond selloff (2Y +12.8bp) is a real-rate repricing, not risk-off - do not treat long gold as a rates hedge into the Warsh September decision.

HBR/Reuters: policy repricing shows up in the 2-yr first — a +12.8bp front-end move against +2.2bp on the 30-yr is a Fed-path signal (Warsh floating a hike), not term premium. Second read: when the hedge breaks harder than the asset it insures (gold -3.4%, silver -4.6% vs S&P -0.25%, VIX 14.4), the metals position was crowded positioning, not protection.

HBR/CNBC: >80% odds on a September Fed HIKE (Warsh, Jackson Hole) landing simultaneously with a US-Iran oil shock (+3.3% to $86) - tightening into a supply shock is the setup that breaks the buy-the-dip reflex.
Wharton x2 + CNBC: long end is repricing sovereign CREDIT, not policy - US 30Y 5.21% vs 3M 3.83% (~138bp term premium), France borrowing costs at near-2008 highs.
CNBC: South Korea -5% following the plunge in US AI-linked names - the AI-equity drawdown now transmits internationally; treat AI-complex correlation as a global channel, not a US sector event.

CNBC: global yields at multi-decade highs (US30Y 5.278, UK10Y 5.252 +0.103, Japan borrowing costs 30-yr high w/ Bessent flagging yen intervention) while S&P only -0.33% but VIX +6.9% - the repricing is in bonds, equities have not marked it yet.

CNBC: oil +2.64% to 88.02 on Iran escalation while gold -1.36% AND silver -2.45% - fear bid absent from metals, so treat this leg as rate/term-premium driven, not geopolitical-risk driven. Divergence is the tell.

HBR Sept-Oct 2026 (Csaszar; Ferreira/Tong) + NBER CentaurBench + HBR Hoque/Davenport converge in one week on augment-vs-automate as the measurable variable; headcount-first AI yields firms 'smaller but not smarter'. Screen AI-capex names on work-redesign evidence, not layoff counts.

Wed Sep 2 pre-open — S&P fell 0.71% to 7,631.47 Tue (third consecutive decline), Nasdaq -1.03% to 26,099.77, Dow -0.79% to 52,766.88. Macro context: US struck IRGC targets inside Iran, Iran fired ballistic missiles at US base in Jordan — full-scale clashes push oil into war-pricing mode (WTI ~$91, Brent ~$96, +5%). 10Y at 4.8% (highest since Oct 2023), 30Y at 5.28%. Fed rate hike odds at 60-66% for September. Gold fell for 3rd consecutive day, Bitcoin below $78K. Warsh's hawkish Jackson Hole + oil-supply shock = the ratchet setup warned about Aug 31. Position: this is the exact tightening-into-supply-shock regime that breaks buy-the-dip reflex. Size down. ACN holds at $188.09 close (Sep 1), portfolio $100,749, BULLISH thesis holding. Day 129/90, 41d overdue. Markets closed until 09:30 ET today.
